title: Built a market data/research platform for traders — looking for people to stress test it
author: deepfit
selftext:
We've spent the last year building a tool called Secmast (secmast.com), and we are soft launching it today.

The basic idea was that I wanted to be able to quickly research and test strategies and signals without spending most of my time finding, cleaning, joining, and wiring together data.

Today we have historical U.S. equity data going back more than 20 years, options history going back to 2013/2014, SEC/EDGAR data, FRED, and we're building a historical securities master that tracks securities, ticker changes, and lineage over time.

Our market datasets currently go down to 1-minute intervals, and we expect to have 1-second intervals, including options, available in the next couple of weeks. The data is already processed; we're waiting on additional hardware to bring it online. Stock intervals include enhanced bid/ask spread fields. Options intervals include IV, first- and second-order Greeks, and additional derived fields.

On top of that is a research agent that can actually work with the data rather than just answer questions from an LLM's training data. It can search filings, query datasets, write and execute Python/Polars analysis, and generate results, charts, and images from the underlying data.

For example, you can ask things like:

* Compare the behavior of SPY options around CPI releases over the last 10 years.
* Find the top institutional holders of a company and how those positions changed.
* Analyze a stock's intraday behavior following earnings surprises.
* Pull a specific metric across years of 10-Ks and compare it with market performance.

You can also describe a strategy and have it test the logic over a specified historical period. There's still a lot we're building, including deeper backtesting support, but the core research/data platform is now live.

I'm posting here because this is probably one of the harder audiences to impress, which is exactly what I'm looking for.

I'd like to give some people free access and see what you try to do with it: what breaks, where the agent makes bad decisions, what data you think is missing, and whether this is actually useful in a real research workflow.

This isn't a "buy my trading bot" post. Secmast doesn't sell signals or strategies, and you can't trade through it. I'm also not claiming it can magically find alpha. It's infrastructure and tooling for doing the research.

I'm one of the founders and core developer, so I'm also happy to answer technical questions about the architecture, data, agent, or why I built particular pieces the way I did.

Feedback — including critical feedback — is very welcome.

The site is secmast.com. If anyone here wants to put it through its paces, DM me. I'm happy to give you some credits or a free membership to experiment with it.

comments.author: veritas7411
comments.body:
I'd be iterested in taking it for a spin! Background: I run an automated research pipeline on US equities, mostly daily and intraday event
studies, with strict reproducibility rules. Some questions for youP: 
1. Is there a raw export or an API, or does everything come out through the
   agent?
2. What's the source and adjustment convention on the equity history, and
   does it change anywhere in the series? 
3. Are the bid/ask fields real NBBO or reconstructed, and what timestamp
   within the bar do they represent? I care specifically about spreads in
   stressed names on high-volume days.
4. Does the securities master carry point-in-time index membership, or only
   ticker lineage? 
5. Are delisted issuers present in the history or dropped? 

If you're still handing out credits or a trial membership, I'll take you up on it, and happy to share feedback with you/your team!

replies.author: deepfit
replies.body:
1. Is there a raw export or an API, or does everything come out through the agent?

No, due to data licensing we can't redistribute the data.  Everything is done by the agent in a sandbox that contains all the data including market bars, SEC, lineage, and alternative datasets preprocessed for accuracy and performance.

2. What's the source and adjustment convention on the equity history, and does it change anywhere in the series?

I have a whole sheet on that and I am happy to share it.  We process from raw SIP.  There are multiple rules and rule changes going back to 2003, which is the start of our tape.  As we get more support pages up I will publish those rules in detail but they are industry standard and handle both regular trading hours and full day.  Each intervals is rolled up independently.

3. Are the bid/ask fields real NBBO or reconstructed, and what timestamp within the bar do they represent? I care specifically about spreads in stressed names on high-volume days.

The bid/ask fields for stocks are real NBBO top of book. The bid-ask spread for options use the stock spread at the closest trade

4. Does the securities master carry point-in-time index membership, or only ticker lineage?

That's interesting.  We are building it around ticker changes including mergers/acquisitions/spin-offs/name-company changes but there is no reason we couldn't add index membership to it.  That was actually the first problem I ran into and why the company is named secmast (security master).

5. Are delisted issuers present in the history or dropped?

Delisted are present.  The bars are point in time data for stocks and options.  Currently unadjusted but that will change soon with the security master database and will have both.  Forex, Crypto, Futures (contracts and continuous), and Indices are all unadjusted.

DM your email when you sign up and I will add on a membership for you.
